ladder.teaches: union by rank and path compression
ladder.why: The whole data structure in its smallest form: union every edge, compare roots; rank and path compression keep 2*10^5 operations fast.
Start with n groups and subtract one for every union that really merges two of them.
An edge whose ends already share a root is redundant, and redundant wires are what you can move.

ladder.teaches: union-find that carries extra data (sizes, weights)
ladder.why: Each root carries its component size, so the longest run is known after every new house.
Components that change online: +1 per new land cell, -1 per merge with a neighbouring island.

ladder.teaches: process edges in sorted order (Kruskal, offline queries)
ladder.why: Kruskal: take edges from cheapest up and keep one only when union-find says it joins two components.

ladder.teaches: union-find that carries extra data (sizes, weights)
ladder.why: Union by size, then score each root by its component size.

ladder.teaches: union-find that carries extra data (sizes, weights)
ladder.why: Roots carry a min and max label instead of a size; merging combines them.

ladder.teaches: union-find that carries extra data (sizes, weights)
ladder.why: Roots carry vertex and edge counts, so each component can be classified as a tree or not.
Revisiting is allowed, so the answer is just the cheapest road in city 1's component.

ladder.teaches: process edges in sorted order (Kruskal, offline queries)
ladder.why: Add roads from the strongest down; the road that first joins start and end is the bottleneck.

ladder.teaches: process edges in sorted order (Kruskal, offline queries)
ladder.why: Sort the logs by time and union until the component count reaches one.

ladder.teaches: union-find that carries extra data (sizes, weights)
ladder.why: Weighted union-find: each node stores its ratio to the root, and queries divide two ratios.

ladder.teaches: process edges in sorted order (Kruskal, offline queries)
ladder.why: Kruskal on 10^5 points, after proving only x-sorted and y-sorted neighbours can be MST edges.
